commands.title: ls -lah
commands.descriptionLong: Shows permissions, owners, sizes, and timestamps for the current directory.

commands.title: ls -lt
commands.descriptionLong: Sorts entries by modification time; hidden files are omitted.

commands.title: ls -lS
commands.descriptionLong: Sorts by file size; directory entry sizes do not measure their contents.

commands.title: cd "<directory>"
commands.descriptionLong: Paste into the terminal where you want to change the working directory.

commands.title: cd ..
commands.descriptionLong: Changes the current terminal's directory one level up.

commands.title: cd ~
commands.descriptionLong: Changes the current terminal's working directory to your home.

commands.title: cd -
commands.descriptionLong: Uses the previous working directory recorded by your current shell.

commands.title: touch -- "<file>"
commands.descriptionShort: Create a file or update its timestamp
commands.descriptionLong: Creates an empty file if absent; an existing file's contents are preserved.

commands.title: mkdir -p -- "<directory>"
commands.descriptionLong: Creates the requested directory tree without failing on existing directories.

commands.title: cp -i -- "<source>" "<destination>"
commands.descriptionShort: Copy a file with overwrite confirmation
commands.descriptionLong: Prompts before replacing an existing destination file.

commands.title: cp -a -i -- "<source-directory>" "<destination>"
commands.descriptionShort: Copy a directory and preserve metadata
commands.descriptionLong: Copies recursively while preserving attributes where possible; prompts before overwriting.

commands.title: mv -i -- "<source>" "<destination>"
commands.descriptionLong: Moves the source and prompts if the destination would be overwritten.

commands.title: rm -i -- "<file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Permanently removes the named file after a prompt; this does not use the desktop trash.

commands.title: rm -rI -- "<directory>"
commands.descriptionShort: Delete a directory with a confirmation prompt
commands.descriptionLong: GNU rm asks once before recursive removal. Review the entire path; deletion is permanent.

commands.title: rmdir -- "<directory>"
commands.descriptionLong: Fails if the directory still contains entries.

commands.title: ln -s -- "<target>" "<link>"
commands.descriptionLong: Creates a link pointing to the target. Relative targets are resolved from the link's directory.

commands.title: readlink -f -- "<path>"
commands.descriptionShort: Resolve a path and symbolic links
commands.descriptionLong: Prints the canonical path using GNU readlink.

commands.title: stat -- "<path>"
commands.descriptionLong: Displays size, ownership, permissions, and filesystem timestamps.

commands.title: file -- "<path>"
commands.descriptionLong: Examines file contents to report the likely type; the file utility may need installation.

commands.title: cat -- "<file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Writes the file to the terminal; use less for large files.

commands.title: cat -n -- "<file>"
commands.descriptionShort: Print a file with line numbers
commands.descriptionLong: Numbers every output line.

commands.title: less -- "<file>"
commands.descriptionShort: Read a file page by page
commands.descriptionLong: Use / to search, n for the next match, and q to quit.

commands.title: head -n 20 -- "<file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Displays the start of a text file without loading an editor.

commands.title: tail -n 50 -- "<file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Useful for inspecting recent entries in a log file.

commands.title: tail -F -- "<file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Waits for new lines and retries when the file is replaced; Ctrl+C stops following.

commands.title: wc -l -- "<file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Counts newline characters; a final line without a newline is not counted.

commands.title: wc -w -- "<file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Reports the number of whitespace-separated words.

commands.title: sort -- "<file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Prints sorted output without changing the input file.

commands.title: sort -n -- "<file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Orders lines by their numeric value rather than alphabetically.

commands.title: sort -u -- "<file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Prints one copy of each distinct line.

commands.title: sort -- "<file>" | uniq -c
commands.descriptionLong: Groups equal lines, then prints their occurrence counts.

commands.title: cut -d ',' -f 1 -- "<file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Splits on literal commas; this is not a full CSV parser for quoted fields.

commands.title: awk '{print $1}' "<file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Reads each line and prints its first field without modifying the file.

commands.title: sed 's/<old>/<new>/g' "<file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Prints transformed text without modifying the file. Escape regex and replacement characters when needed.

commands.title: sed -i.bak 's/<old>/<new>/g' "<file>"
commands.descriptionShort: Replace text while keeping a backup
commands.descriptionLong: GNU sed edits the file and keeps its previous contents in a .bak file. An existing backup may be replaced.

commands.title: diff -u -- "<first-file>" "<second-file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Shows a unified diff; exit status 1 means differences were found.

commands.title: printf '%s\n' "<text>" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'
commands.descriptionLong: Prints converted text without writing to a file.

commands.title: tee -a "<file>"
commands.descriptionShort: Append typed input to a file
commands.descriptionLong: Copies standard input to the terminal and appends it to the file; Ctrl+D ends input.

commands.title: find . -type f -name '*.txt'
commands.descriptionLong: Searches from the current directory. Quotes keep the shell from expanding the wildcard first.

commands.title: find . -type f -iname '*<name>*'
commands.descriptionLong: Replace the name fragment, keeping the wildcard pattern quoted.

commands.title: find . -type d -name '<name>'
commands.descriptionLong: Searches recursively for directories with the specified name.

commands.title: find . -type f -mtime -7
commands.descriptionShort: Find files modified in the last week
commands.descriptionLong: Uses elapsed 24-hour periods from the current time.

commands.title: find . -type f -size +100M
commands.descriptionLong: Searches beneath the current directory without changing files.

commands.title: find . -type f -empty
commands.descriptionLong: Lists regular files with no contents.

commands.title: grep -nF -- "<text>" "<file>"
commands.descriptionShort: Find literal text with line numbers
commands.descriptionLong: Treats the search text as a fixed string rather than a regular expression.

commands.title: grep -niF -- "<text>" "<file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Prints matching lines and their line numbers.

commands.title: grep -rInF -- "<text>" "<directory>"
commands.descriptionLong: Searches recursively, skips binary files, and shows line numbers.

commands.title: grep -vF -- "<text>" "<file>"
commands.descriptionShort: Show lines that do not contain text
commands.descriptionLong: Prints the nonmatching lines without editing the file.

commands.title: grep -E -- "<regex>" "<file>"
commands.descriptionShort: Search with an extended regular expression
commands.descriptionLong: Use regular expression syntax for the pattern.

commands.title: rg -n -- "<pattern>" "<directory>"
commands.descriptionLong: Respects ignore files by default; requires ripgrep.

commands.title: rg --hidden -g '!.git' -- "<pattern>" .
commands.descriptionLong: Includes hidden files while excluding the .git directory; requires ripgrep.

commands.title: locate "<name>"
commands.descriptionLong: Requires a locate implementation and an up-to-date index; recently created files may be absent.

commands.title: type -a "<command>"
commands.descriptionShort: Find command definitions in your shell
commands.descriptionLong: Shows matching aliases, builtins, functions, and executable locations in the current shell.

commands.title: tar -czf "<archive>.tar.gz" -- "<directory>"
commands.descriptionLong: Writes a gzip-compressed archive. An existing archive at that path is overwritten.

commands.title: tar -tzf "<archive>.tar.gz"
commands.descriptionLong: Inspects filenames without extracting files.

commands.title: tar -xzf "<archive>.tar.gz" -C "<destination>"
commands.descriptionLong: The destination must exist. Use an empty destination and review the archive before extraction.

commands.title: tar -cf "<archive>.tar" -- "<directory>"
commands.descriptionLong: Stores the directory tree in an archive; an existing archive is overwritten.

commands.title: tar -xf "<archive>" -C "<destination>"
commands.descriptionLong: GNU tar recognizes common compression formats. The destination must already exist.

commands.title: zip -r "<archive>.zip" "<directory>"
commands.descriptionLong: Creates or updates the archive; requires zip.

commands.title: unzip -l "<archive>.zip"
commands.descriptionLong: Shows file names and sizes without extracting; requires unzip.

commands.title: unzip -n "<archive>.zip" -d "<destination>"
commands.descriptionLong: Creates the destination as needed and skips existing files.

commands.title: gzip -k -- "<file>"
commands.descriptionShort: Compress a file and retain the original
commands.descriptionLong: Writes a .gz file while keeping the source file.

commands.title: gunzip -k -- "<file>.gz"
commands.descriptionShort: Decompress and retain the compressed file
commands.descriptionLong: Writes the uncompressed file while keeping the .gz input.

commands.title: xz -k -- "<file>"
commands.descriptionShort: Compress with xz and keep the original
commands.descriptionLong: Creates a .xz file; requires xz and can use significant CPU time.

commands.title: sha256sum -- "<file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Use to compare a downloaded file with a trusted published checksum.

commands.title: sha256sum -c "<checksums-file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Reads expected hashes and filenames from a checksum file.

commands.title: ls -ld -- "<path>"
commands.descriptionLong: Shows the path's own permissions rather than listing a directory's contents.

commands.title: chmod u+x -- "<script>"
commands.descriptionShort: Make a script executable for its owner
commands.descriptionLong: Adds owner execute permission without changing other permission bits.

commands.title: chmod 600 -- "<file>"
commands.descriptionShort: Restrict a file to its owner
commands.descriptionLong: Allows owner read and write only; useful for a private file.

commands.title: chmod 644 -- "<file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Owner can read and write; group and others can read.

commands.title: chmod 755 -- "<directory>"
commands.descriptionLong: Owner can modify entries; others can list and traverse the directory.

commands.title: chmod u-x -- "<file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Changes only the owner's execute bit.

commands.title: sudo chown "<user>:<group>" -- "<path>"
commands.descriptionLong: Changes the owner and group; applies only to the specified path.

commands.title: chgrp "<group>" -- "<path>"
commands.descriptionLong: You need appropriate ownership and group membership.

commands.title: umask
commands.descriptionLong: Displays which permission bits the current shell removes when creating files.

commands.title: getfacl -- "<path>"
commands.descriptionLong: Shows additional ACL permissions when supported; requires the acl utilities.

commands.title: whoami
commands.descriptionLong: Prints the account name used for the current command.

commands.title: id
commands.descriptionShort: Show your user and group IDs
commands.descriptionLong: Displays the current account's numeric IDs and group memberships.

commands.title: id "<user>"
commands.descriptionLong: Shows the account's UID, primary group, and supplementary groups.

commands.title: groups
commands.descriptionLong: Reports the current process's groups; newly added memberships may require a fresh login.

commands.title: getent passwd "<user>"
commands.descriptionLong: Queries configured account sources, including network directories if configured.

commands.title: who
commands.descriptionLong: Lists login sessions recorded by the system.

commands.title: w
commands.descriptionLong: Shows logged-in users, their activity, and system load.

commands.title: passwd
commands.descriptionLong: Prompts securely in the terminal; do not put passwords into saved commands.

commands.title: sudo useradd -m "<username>"
commands.descriptionShort: Create a user with a home directory
commands.descriptionLong: Creates the account and home directory. Configure a password separately if needed.

commands.title: sudo usermod -aG "<group>" "<username>"
commands.descriptionShort: Add a user to a supplementary group
commands.descriptionLong: The -a flag preserves other group memberships. Some groups grant powerful system access.

commands.title: sudo passwd "<username>"
commands.descriptionLong: Prompts in the terminal and requires administrator privileges.

commands.title: sudo userdel "<username>"
commands.descriptionLong: Removes the account but keeps the home directory; check running sessions first.

commands.title: uname -a
commands.descriptionLong: Prints kernel release, architecture, and related system information.

commands.title: cat /etc/os-release
commands.descriptionLong: Displays the distribution's name and version metadata.

commands.title: lscpu
commands.descriptionLong: Shows processor model, cores, threads, and architecture details.

commands.title: hostnamectl
commands.descriptionLong: Uses systemd to show host identity and operating system information.

commands.title: date -Is
commands.descriptionShort: Print the current date and time
commands.descriptionLong: Uses ISO 8601 format with the local timezone offset.

commands.title: timedatectl
commands.descriptionLong: Shows timezone and time synchronization status on systemd systems.

commands.title: lsusb
commands.descriptionLong: Requires usbutils; shows connected devices without changing them.

commands.title: lspci
commands.descriptionLong: Requires pciutils; useful for identifying graphics, network, and storage hardware.

commands.title: vmstat 1 5
commands.descriptionLong: Prints five reports at one-second intervals; the first report includes averages since boot.

commands.title: sudo dmesg --level=err,warn
commands.descriptionLong: May require administrator privileges because kernel logs are restricted.

commands.title: nano "<file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Ctrl+O saves, Enter confirms the filename, and Ctrl+X exits. Requires nano.

commands.title: vim "<file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Press i to insert text; Esc then :wq saves and exits, while :q! discards changes.

commands.title: man "<command>"
commands.descriptionLong: Use / to search and q to quit the usual pager. Manual packages may need installation.

commands.title: apropos "<keyword>"
commands.descriptionLong: Searches manual page summaries; the local manual index must be available.

commands.title: help cd
commands.descriptionLong: Run in Bash to see help for its cd builtin.

commands.title: curl -I "<url>"
commands.descriptionLong: Sends a HEAD request. Some servers handle HEAD differently from GET.

commands.title: curl --fail --show-error --location "<url>"
commands.descriptionShort: Fetch a URL and follow redirects
commands.descriptionLong: Prints the response and reports HTTP errors. TLS certificate verification remains enabled.

commands.title: curl --fail --location --output "<file>" "<url>"
commands.descriptionLong: Writes the response to the chosen file; an existing file can be overwritten.

commands.title: curl --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 15 -I "<url>"
commands.descriptionShort: Check a URL with time limits
commands.descriptionLong: Limits connection setup to five seconds and the complete request to fifteen seconds.

commands.title: wget -c "<url>"
commands.descriptionLong: Attempts to continue an existing download; verify the resulting file when the remote content may have changed.

commands.title: dig "<domain>"
commands.descriptionLong: Requires DNS tools such as bind-utils on Fedora or dnsutils on Debian.

commands.title: dig +short "<domain>" A
commands.descriptionLong: Prints concise answers for the domain's A record query.

commands.title: nslookup "<domain>"
commands.descriptionLong: Queries DNS using a tool provided by your distribution's DNS utility package.

commands.title: ip -brief link
commands.descriptionLong: Shows interface names, MAC addresses, and link status.

commands.title: ip route get "<ip-address>"
commands.descriptionShort: Show the route to an address
commands.descriptionLong: Reports the interface and source address the kernel would use.

commands.title: ss -ltnp
commands.descriptionLong: Shows processes where permissions allow; extra privileges may reveal more process details.

commands.title: nmcli connection show
commands.descriptionLong: Uses NetworkManager without exposing stored Wi-Fi passwords.

commands.title: traceroute "<host>"
commands.descriptionLong: Requires traceroute; filtering can hide intermediate hops.

commands.title: ssh -i "<private-key>" "<user>@<host>"
commands.descriptionShort: Connect using a specific SSH key
commands.descriptionLong: Uses an existing private key file; verify the server host key on first connection.

commands.title: ssh -p <port> "<user>@<host>"
commands.descriptionShort: Connect to a custom SSH port
commands.descriptionLong: Replace the port with the server's SSH listening port.

commands.title: ssh -N -L 1420:127.0.0.1:1420 "<user>@<host>"
commands.descriptionShort: Forward a remote web preview locally
commands.descriptionLong: Run on the device that opens the browser. While connected, its localhost:1420 forwards to the remote host's localhost:1420.

commands.title: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "<label>"
commands.descriptionLong: Prompts for a filename and passphrase. Use a new filename to avoid replacing an existing key.

commands.title: ssh-copy-id "<user>@<host>"
commands.descriptionShort: Install your public key on a server
commands.descriptionLong: Adds a local public key to the remote account after authentication; verify the target account first.

commands.title: scp -r "<directory>" "<user>@<host>:<destination>"
commands.descriptionLong: Transfers the directory recursively; remote destination files may be overwritten.

commands.title: rsync -avhn -- "<source>/" "<destination>/"
commands.descriptionLong: Dry run: lists proposed transfers without changing files. The trailing source slash means its contents.

commands.title: htop
commands.descriptionLong: Requires htop. Use its controls to inspect processes; q exits.

commands.title: ps -ef
commands.descriptionLong: Shows a full process listing including the parent process ID.

commands.title: ps -p <pid> -o pid,ppid,user,etime,args
commands.descriptionLong: Displays identity, elapsed time, and the command line for the selected PID.

commands.title: kill -TERM <pid>
commands.descriptionLong: Sends SIGTERM so the application has an opportunity to clean up. Check the PID first.

commands.title: kill -KILL <pid>
commands.descriptionLong: Use only after graceful termination fails; the process cannot save data or clean up.

commands.title: pgrep -af -- "<pattern>"
commands.descriptionShort: Find processes by full command line
commands.descriptionLong: Prints matching process IDs and commands; the pattern is a regular expression.

commands.title: lsof -i :<port>
commands.descriptionLong: Requires lsof; visibility of other users' processes depends on privileges.

commands.title: watch -n 2 'df -h'
commands.descriptionLong: Refreshes the display every two seconds; Ctrl+C exits.

commands.title: sudo systemctl start "<service>"
commands.descriptionLong: Starts the selected service now without changing its boot setting.

commands.title: sudo systemctl stop "<service>"
commands.descriptionLong: Stops the selected service and may interrupt dependent applications.

commands.title: sudo systemctl restart "<service>"
commands.descriptionLong: Stops and starts the service; expect an interruption.

commands.title: sudo systemctl enable --now "<service>"
commands.descriptionShort: Start a service and enable it at boot
commands.descriptionLong: Changes boot configuration and starts the service immediately.

commands.title: sudo systemctl disable "<service>"
commands.descriptionShort: Prevent a service from starting at boot
commands.descriptionLong: Changes its enablement links; a running service is not stopped by this command.

commands.title: sudo systemctl daemon-reload
commands.descriptionLong: Use after changing unit files. This does not itself restart services.

commands.title: systemctl cat "<service>"
commands.descriptionShort: Read a service unit and overrides
commands.descriptionLong: Displays the unit files systemd uses for the selected service.

commands.title: journalctl -u "<service>" -f
commands.descriptionLong: Streams new log entries for the selected unit; Ctrl+C stops following.

commands.title: journalctl --since '1 hour ago'
commands.descriptionLong: Shows entries from the last hour that your account can access.

commands.title: journalctl -b -1
commands.descriptionLong: Requires journal data to have been retained from the preceding boot.

commands.title: journalctl -k -b
commands.descriptionShort: Read kernel logs from this boot
commands.descriptionLong: Filters the journal to kernel messages for the current boot.

commands.title: du -h --max-depth=1 -- "<directory>"
commands.descriptionLong: GNU du reports disk usage one level below the chosen directory.

commands.title: df -hT
commands.descriptionLong: Lists capacity and mount information with human-readable units.

commands.title: lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINTS
commands.descriptionLong: Shows devices, filesystem types, and their mount points.

commands.title: printenv PATH
commands.descriptionLong: Prints the PATH value inherited by this command.

commands.title: printenv
commands.descriptionLong: Values can contain credentials; review the output before sharing it.

commands.title: export <NAME>='<value>'
commands.descriptionShort: Set a variable in your current shell
commands.descriptionLong: Paste into the terminal whose environment you want to change; values are inherited by child processes.

commands.title: unset <NAME>
commands.descriptionLong: Affects the shell in which you paste the command.

commands.title: source ~/.bashrc
commands.descriptionLong: Executes the contents of your .bashrc in the current Bash session.

commands.title: alias ll='ls -lah'
commands.descriptionLong: Defines the alias for the current shell; save it in shell configuration to keep it across sessions.

commands.title: unalias ll
commands.descriptionLong: Affects the current shell if that alias exists.

commands.title: history 20
commands.descriptionLong: Shows recent commands from the current interactive shell; history may contain sensitive values.

commands.title: jobs -l
commands.descriptionLong: Shows jobs started by the current interactive shell, including process IDs.

commands.title: fg %1
commands.descriptionLong: Uses job number 1 from the current shell's jobs list.

commands.title: bg %1
commands.descriptionShort: Resume suspended job 1 in the background
commands.descriptionLong: The job remains associated with the current shell.

commands.title: printf '%s\n' "<text>" > "<file>"
commands.descriptionLong: The redirection replaces the destination's contents. Review the filename first.

commands.title: printf '%s\n' "<text>" >> "<file>"
commands.descriptionLong: Creates the file if needed and preserves existing contents.

commands.title: dnf search "<package>"
commands.descriptionLong: Searches package metadata without installing software.

commands.title: sudo dnf install "<package>"
commands.descriptionLong: Review the transaction and dependencies before confirming.

commands.title: sudo dnf remove "<package>"
commands.descriptionLong: Review dependent packages selected for removal before confirming.

commands.title: apt search "<package>"
commands.descriptionLong: Searches available package descriptions without installing anything.

commands.title: sudo apt install "<package>"
commands.descriptionShort: Install a Debian or Ubuntu package
commands.descriptionLong: Review the proposed transaction before confirming.

commands.title: sudo apt remove "<package>"
commands.descriptionShort: Remove a Debian or Ubuntu package
commands.descriptionLong: Removes the package while generally retaining its configuration files.

commands.title: sudo pacman -S "<package>"
commands.descriptionLong: Use an up-to-date system; Arch does not support partial upgrades.

commands.title: sudo pacman -R "<package>"
commands.descriptionLong: Review the removal transaction before confirming.

commands.title: sudo zypper install "<package>"
commands.descriptionLong: Resolves dependencies and asks for transaction confirmation.

commands.title: sudo zypper remove "<package>"
commands.descriptionLong: Review the packages listed for removal before confirming.

commands.title: flatpak search "<application>"
commands.descriptionLong: Searches configured remotes for matching applications.

commands.title: flatpak install flathub "<application-id>"
commands.descriptionLong: Requires the Flathub remote; review application permissions before confirming.

commands.title: flatpak uninstall "<application-id>"
commands.descriptionLong: Removes the selected application; review the transaction before confirming.

commands.title: sudo apk update
commands.descriptionLong: Requires Alpine Linux and sudo configured for your account; root shells can omit sudo.

commands.title: sudo apk upgrade
commands.descriptionLong: Review system compatibility before updating; requires administrator privileges.

commands.title: apk search "<package>"
commands.descriptionLong: Searches the available package indexes.

commands.title: sudo apk add "<package>"
commands.descriptionLong: Adds the package and its dependencies; requires administrator privileges.

commands.title: sudo apk del "<package>"
commands.descriptionLong: Removes the selected package and dependencies no longer required by the package manager.
